profile.summary: FrameDiff generates new protein backbones from noise. It represents each residue as a rigid body (a frame: a position and an orientation in 3D) and runs a diffusion model over those frames. The output is a set of monomer backbone structures in PDB format at the requested lengths, which can then be given sequences with a design tool such as ProteinMPNN.

summary_quotes.text: a diffusion model over rigid bodies in 3D (referred to as frames) has shown success in generating novel, functional protein backbones
a novel framework, FrameDiff, for learning the SE(3) equivariant score over multiple frames
We apply FrameDiff on monomer backbone generation and find it can generate designable monomers up to 500 amino acids without relying on a pretrained protein structure prediction network

sections.title: How it works
sections.body: The authors develop a diffusion model on SE(3), the space of rotations and translations, applied to one frame per residue. Noise is added separately to translations (an R(3) diffuser) and rotations (an SO(3) diffuser), and a network learns the SE(3) equivariant score used to reverse the noise. In the released configuration the score network has 4 blocks of invariant point attention layers with 8 heads and a 2-layer sequence transformer, node embedding 256 and edge embedding 128. The repository keeps a modified fork of OpenFold. FrameDiff does not rely on a pretrained structure prediction network. Sampling uses 500 steps by default.

sections.title: Versions and reproducibility
sections.body: The repository holds two weight files. weights/paper_weights.pth gives the ICML paper results and is loaded by default. weights/best_weights.pth is a fine-tuned model produced after a bug fix in the rotation score, dated 27 June 2023 in the README. Matching configs are config/icml_published.yaml and config/base.yaml. The authors report preliminary designability of 0.29 for the published settings and 0.34 for base.yaml; those are their numbers. A result should name the weight file and the config used. This page read the repository at commit 53359d71.

quotes.text: The weights used to get the `icml_published.yaml` results are in `weights/paper_weights.pth` while the weights to get the `base.yaml`results are in `weights/best_weights.pth`.

facts.label: Architecture
facts.value: SE(3) diffusion over per-residue frames, with separate translation (R(3)) and rotation (SO(3)) diffusers. Score network of 4 blocks with 8 attention heads and a 2-layer sequence transformer, node embedding 256, edge embedding 128.

quotes.text: a novel framework, FrameDiff, for learning the SE(3) equivariant score over multiple frames

facts.label: Inputs
facts.value: No structure or sequence input. The user sets the lengths to sample, by default 100 to 500 in steps of 5, and the number of samples per length.

facts.label: Outputs
facts.value: Backbone PDB files per sample, the diffusion trajectory, and self-consistency results: ProteinMPNN sequences, ESMFold predictions and a metrics CSV.

run_guide.summary: Install the conda environment from the pinned commit and sample protein backbones with the published weights.
prerequisites: Conda or miniconda, as the README recommends.
A CUDA GPU: the environment file pins cuda 11.6 and the inference config takes a gpu_id.
A local copy of ProteinMPNN for the self-consistency step: the inference config points pmpnn_dir at ./ProteinMPNN/.
Disk space for the samples; the default run covers lengths 100 to 500 with 10 samples each.

steps.title: Sample backbones
steps.explanation: Runs the inference script with config/inference.yaml. It loads weights/paper_weights.pth, runs 500 diffusion steps and writes samples under ./inference_outputs/.

outputs: A dated folder under ./inference_outputs/ holding the config used and, per length and sample, the final backbone PDB, the diffusion trajectories and a self_consistency folder with ProteinMPNN sequences, ESMFold predictions and sc_results.csv.

The self-consistency step needs ProteinMPNN in the path set by pmpnn_dir; the README does not give its install steps.

notes: The official repository is named se3_diffusion; FrameDiff is the method name used in the paper and in the repository's own landing image. The record's description says released 2023-03, while the arXiv submission history shows v1 on 5 February 2023; no release date is recorded in structured because no source states one for the checkpoints. Only the arXiv abstract page was read, not the full paper. The context_length value of 500 residues is the longest generated length the abstract reports and the default maximum sampled length, not a hard architectural limit.
